title: Write-ahead buy intent row and synchronous=FULL (schema 7 to 8), and what the first shutdown signal does with an in-flight buy

options.name: Keep current behaviour: the buy row is written only after the submission returns, the first shutdown signal closes the DB and exits at once, synchronous=NORMAL
options.risk: A buy that lands while the bot is stopped or crashes inside its multi-minute submission window is held with no row: no exit monitor, no anti-rug watch, no dedup record (AUD-DB-004); a power loss can roll back the last committed rows.

options.name: Switch to synchronous=FULL only
options.behavior_impact: One fsync per commit; rows survive a power loss or OS crash.
options.risk: Does nothing for the stop/crash window, which is the larger exposure.

options.name: First signal waits (up to SIGINT_GRACE_MS) for in-flight buys to finish and write their row before closing the DB; no schema change
options.behavior_impact: A routine stop no longer loses a landing buy; stopping can take up to the grace period.
options.risk: Crashes and force-kills (taskkill, a second signal, the grace timeout) still lose the row.

options.name: Write an intent row (token, chain, nonce, signed hashes) before the first submission, reconcile intents against the chain at boot (schema 8), add the shutdown drain and synchronous=FULL
options.behavior_impact: Every landed buy is either recorded or found at the next boot; a routine stop waits for in-flight buys.
options.risk: A schema migration (7 to 8) and boot reconciliation on the money path; must be proven on a fork before live use; the newer-schema guard (22-09) then blocks a rollback to an older build.

recommendation: Research recommendation (research SUMMARY OD-18): synchronous=FULL (negligible cost); the intent row only if the audit confirms the crash window. The audit confirms the window and finds the routine shutdown path inside it (AUD-DB-004), which matches intent-row-and-full.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract). This card covers S1 capital findings, which cannot rest on the default: until it is decided and fixed it blocks the live re-entry gate.
behavior_impact: Decides whether a buy can land without the bot knowing about it, how a stop treats an in-flight buy, and the database durability mode.
needed_by: Phase 24 discussion before Wave A (capital fixes, after the Phase 23 real-path proof)
